answer:
The diversity in Pottery Form collapses while the diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneously in the **17th century BCE (around 1700 BCE)**.

Hypothesis (natural language): Between the 1800 BCE and 1700 BCE records, pottery-form diversity drops sharply from its Late Neolithic/Early Bronze Age level (Z = 0.74) to the minimum of the entire record (Z = −1.13), where it then remains flat, while pottery-decoration diversity jumps from below average (Z = −0.48) to well above average (Z = 0.97, later reaching 1.53). This is the only 100-year step in the dataset where form diversity falls and decoration diversity rises at the same time, and it is by far the largest such co-movement. I therefore identify the collapse/increase event with the 17th century BCE (the century in which the collapsed-form / high-decoration state is first observed, at the 1700 BCE data point).

Convention used: I assign the event to the century containing the data point where the collapsed state first appears — 1700 BCE is the first year of the 17th century BCE (1700–1601 BCE). Under the alternative convention of attributing the event to the transition interval (1800–1701 BCE), it would fall in the 18th century BCE; I report that as the main uncertainty. The evidence (a single discrete data point at 1700 BCE marking the new state) supports the 17th-century BCE reading.

payload.hypothesis: Pottery-form diversity collapses and pottery-decoration diversity increase simultaneously in the 17th century BCE (~1700 BCE): PotteryForm falls from Z=0.74 (1800 BCE) to Z=-1.13 (1700 BCE, the record minimum) while PotteryDecoration rises from Z=-0.48 to Z=0.97.
payload.workflow: Loaded the raw 100-year pottery series (PotteryForm, PotteryDecoration) from time_series_data.csv (37 real points, CE -4100 to -500). Computed consecutive 100-yr deltas dForm and dDeco. Selecting steps where dForm<0 AND dDeco>0 yielded exactly ONE candidate: the 1800->1700 BCE step (dForm=-1.87, dDeco=+1.45). Validated against the _inter columns (identical at all century steps) and against capital.csv (ZKeform/Zkeverz match on 37/37 shared BCE points). Mapped 1700 BCE to the 17th century BCE.
